claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has superior tribo-corrosion resistance compared with DS2205 duplex stainless steel.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a dual-phase microstructure consisting of BCC-B2 and FCC-L12 phases.
Micro-galvanic coupling occurs between the two phases of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA during molten-salt corrosion.
The FCC-L12 phase is enriched in noble elements and acts as a protective barrier.
The protective FCC-L12 phase reduces selective dissolution of the BCC-B2 phase.
Under high-temperature tribo-corrosion, the FCC-L12 phase reduces oxidation.
Under high-temperature tribo-corrosion, the FCC-L12 phase limits mechanical wear by preventing accelerated phase dissolution.
Micro-galvanic coupling between the phases creates a protective surface layer that mitigates degradation.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA undergoes selective dissolution of its B2 phase during molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 corrosion.
Selective dissolution of B2 in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA is attributable to micro-galvanic coupling between its phases.
In molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 at 450 °C, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a corrosion rate of approximately 1 mm/year compared with approximately 8 mm/year for DS2205.
In molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 at 650 °C, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a corrosion rate of approximately 9 mm/year compared with approximately 20 mm/year for DS2205.
Under combined molten-salt exposure and sliding wear, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA will have lower mass loss than DS2205.
Under combined molten-salt exposure and sliding wear, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA will develop shallower wear tracks than DS2205.
The molten-salt corrosion advantage of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA over DS2205 can be extended to combined tribo-corrosion conditions.
The combined effects of mechanical wear and molten-salt corrosion on this EHEA are less explored than corrosion alone.
